title: Year 7 assessment tracker
subject: English
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 61 (Year 7 assessment tracker)
intro: Lesson 61: Summative assessment: poetry, unseen non-fiction and grammar. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: The assessment
points: Section A: one poem question, choose one of two (12 marks)
Section B: compare two short unseen texts (10 marks)
Section C: grammar and vocabulary (8 marks)

head: Text A: a blog post
Text B: a school guide
rows: 'The first time someone said my name right, I felt I lived here.'
'Learn how to say every new pupil's name correctly.'

keywords.def: an assessment at the end of a unit that shows what you have learned
a text you have not studied before

questions.q: Before the timer: underline the key words in Section A option 1
questions.a: Option 1: 'How does Zephaniah present belonging in The British?': key words 'belonging', 'The British', 'present'.

questions.q: Core (timed, 16 minutes): Section A. Answer ONE: 1) How does Zephaniah present belonging in The British? or 2) How does Hughes present resilience in Mother to Son? Use PETZAAL (12)
questions.a: Marked to the mark scheme: a clear point; accurate quotations from memory (e.g. 'Serve with justice'; 'no crystal stair'); named method (extended metaphor, imperative, dialect); zoom on a word; analysis of effect; an alternative reading; a link to the message.

questions.q: Extend (timed, 11 minutes): Section B. 3) Compare how Text A and Text B present the importance of names (PEEDL) (10)
questions.a: Both see names as part of belonging; Text A through a personal moment ('I felt I lived here'), Text B through instructions; purpose: share a feeling versus guide behaviour; comparative connectives.

questions.q: Stretch (timed, 7 minutes): Section C. 4) Label simile or metaphor: 'Hope is a lighthouse.' (1) 5) Turn into first person plural: 'They welcomed the new family.' (1) 6) Add parallelism: 'We listen, we learn, ...' (1) 7) Correct: 'the poets message is clear, it is about hope' (2) 8) Use 'resilience', 'heritage' and 'legacy' correctly in sentences (3)
questions.a: 4) metaphor. 5) We welcomed the new family. 6) e.g. 'we lead.' 7) The poet's message is clear: it is about hope. (or two sentences) 8) three accurate sentences.

questions.q: For Section A, which question plan is best?
options: choose the poem I know best and plan three points in two minutes
write about all four poems briefly
start writing without reading the question
questions.a: A) choose the poem I know best and plan three points in two minutes. Choice and a quick plan give a focused, developed answer.
